title: Microsoft says months-old bug caused global Microsoft 365 outage
content_md: Microsoft says a software bug introduced in July caused last week's worldwide Microsoft 365 outage, triggering a cascading failure that left more than 80% of its networking gateway servers unresponsive. The nearly 24-hour outage on November 12 disrupted Microsoft 365 services worldwide , including Outlook, Exchange Online, Teams, and Copilot, leaving users unable to access their email and causing significant delays in message delivery. In a preliminary post-incident report shared in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center, the company said the outage was caused by three problems: a previously undetected software bug, increased traffic after a Microsoft Teams failover, and reduced server capacity. The incident began at 11:20 AM ET on Thursday, November 12, and continued until 11:10 AM ET the following day, when Microsoft confirmed that services were full restored. According to Microsoft, the software bug was introduced in July through an update developed for Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers. While the update had been deployed for more than three months without issues, it contained a bug that could overwhelm servers under certain traffic conditions, causing them to stop responding. Microsoft says its tests of the update did not detect the bug as it used less powerful testing hardware than the production servers.
